description.en-US: The module that raised this notification, for example 'sales'. Recorded rather than resolved: Notification never calls back into the source module (BR 30).
The source resource, for example 'sales_order'. Historical metadata only.

Identifier of the source record, as JSON so a composite key fits. A SOFT REFERENCE with no foreign key (BR 31): the source record may be archived or deleted later, and the notification must survive it and must never block that deletion.

Caller-supplied replay guard, unique per org and source module. THE PARTIAL UNIQUE IS THE MECHANISM: a retried send, or a command bus redelivery carrying the same command id, finds the stored notification instead of raising a second one (BR 11.15, BR 12). Strict rather than loose, because the key is the value being constrained and not a scope: most notifications have none, and a loose index would permit only one such notification per module.
Presentation severity. Defaults to 'info' when the sender omits it (BR 11.4).
Calculated, never sent by the caller: 'all' when the sender named no channel, 'explicit' when it did (BR 11.5, BR 11.6).
The channels the sender asked for, meaningful only when distribution_mode is 'explicit'. Null for 'all', which resolves against the organization's enabled channels at send time.
Opaque payload passed through to the client untouched.
After this instant no NEW external delivery is attempted (BR 28). Expiry never deletes the notification, never marks it read, and never rewrites a delivery that already happened.
